question.text: For a Cat III AIF that discharges tax on income at the fund level (representative assessee), which of the following best describes the TDS obligation ON DISTRIBUTION to a resident individual investor?

answer.text: 10% TDS under Section 194LBB on all distributions
Nil — Section 194LBB does not apply to Cat III; fund-level tax has already been discharged, so no separate withholding on distribution

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 194LBB withholds only on 'Investment Funds' as defined under Section 115UB — i.e., Cat I and II. Cat III is outside Section 115UB. Because the fund has discharged MMR tax as representative assessee, distribution to the investor carries no further TDS burden for the fund (subject to redemption being treated as transfer). The Trap: A is the Cat I/II answer and the most seductive distractor — many candidates blindly transplant 194LBB to Cat III. C (194J on professional fees) and D (115A on NR) are unrelated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II) correctly marks 194LBB as 10%/20%. XIX-E MUST contradict this for Cat III. Watch for cross-wired answers in hybrid XIX-C (All-Cat) questions where context governs. Manager's Pro-Tip: When preparing Form 64C/64D and LP statements at Himalaya, put a prominent note that the fund has paid tax at source (fund level) and no TDS under 194LBB applies — preempts 26AS queries from LPs who compare their reports with Cat I/II peers.
